question: Can choosing the resolution γ and temporal coupling ω on an earlier validation window give communities that better explain later interactions than the default γ=1, ω=1 setting on a public temporal messaging network?
method: Time-ordered 60/20/20 split of CollegeMsg messages. Multilayer Louvain communities are built on the training window; γ, ω are selected on the validation window by intra-community fraction minus a partition-instability penalty; the test window is scored once for both models over seeds 42-44.
baseline: Multilayer (Mucha-style) Louvain over time slices with default γ=1 and ω=1.
improved: Same multilayer Louvain, with γ and ω chosen from a small grid by maximizing validation-window intra-community fraction penalized by seed instability (1 - ARI).
notes: Louvain is applied to the whole supra-graph with a single resolution parameter, an approximation of Mucha's layer-wise null model; this is not the LAGO algorithm of the motivating paper. Interactions are treated as undirected and unweighted by direction. Communities are fixed from the training window; each user takes its label from the latest training slice; users unseen in training are singletons. The validation window is a time-ordered part of the non-test data, never the test set. Single dataset, small grid, 3 seeds; differences may be small relative to seed variation.
